title: Where do your tips go?
reason: 昨天的课程围绕记忆与学习方法，今天轮换到金融消费和数字支付。本集讨论餐厅小费如何收集、分配和计税，以及现金支付转向银行卡支付后出现的透明度与公平问题，适合联系金融科技中的资金流向、规则设计和利益分配。练习优先选择可迁移到项目治理、制度说明和工作沟通的高频表达，并通过重复调用逐步进入主动输出。

targetExpressions.meaning: not true in every situation, even if people often expect it to be true
targetExpressions.usage: Use it to correct a common assumption: Faster delivery usually costs more, but that is not always the case.

targetExpressions.meaning: have an established process or arrangement ready to operate
targetExpressions.usage: Use it for existing procedures: We have a system in place for reviewing production changes.

targetExpressions.meaning: in a way that helps or gives an advantage to someone
targetExpressions.usage: Use it when discussing who gains from a decision: The new process should work to the benefit of both users and support staff.

targetExpressions.meaning: be forced on someone without giving them a real choice
targetExpressions.usage: Use it for unwanted rules or duties: Extra reporting requirements were imposed on the team.

targetExpressions.meaning: gradually change or develop in a particular direction
targetExpressions.usage: Use it for an ongoing transition: The department is moving towards automated deployment.

targetExpressions.meaning: collect tips and service charges together before distributing them
targetExpressions.usage: Use it for a shared collection: The restaurant pools tips and service charges before paying staff.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the contrast: Customers may think the waiter who brought the food receives the tip, but that is ______.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript directly challenges the assumption that the person serving the food always keeps the money.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the description: Different restaurants ______ for handling tips.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The programme says restaurants and businesses have different systems in place across the country.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the programme's concern: The different arrangements are not always ______ all waiting staff.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The waiter describes receiving only a small share of the tips he contributed, showing that some systems do not benefit all staff fairly.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: What does it mean if a rule is “imposed on” a worker?

options.text: The worker is forced to accept it.
The worker freely designs it alone.
The rule applies only when the worker requests it.
The rule has been permanently cancelled.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript defines imposed as forced upon someone rather than freely chosen.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete Kate Nicholls's description: Society is ______ cashless payments, with greater use of credit cards.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The speaker says society is moving towards cashless payment, especially after increased card use during the pandemic.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: What happens when a business pools tips and service charges?

options.text: It collects them together before distributing the money.
It immediately returns every payment to the customer.
It converts all tips into restaurant vouchers.
It prevents kitchen staff from receiving any share.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Pool means collect together or group; the tronc arrangement then distributes the shared amount.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Why can a tronc arrangement improve the handling of card-based tips?

options.text: It uses a separate arrangement to collect the money, apply the correct tax treatment and distribute it fairly.
It makes every customer legally required to leave a tip.
It guarantees that only managers receive the money.
It removes all records of digital payments.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript explains that a tronc keeps tips in a separate account, avoids the wrong tax rate and supports fair distribution.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Which sentence uses “have a system in place” naturally in a project context?

options.text: We have a system in place for approving emergency changes.
We system in place the emergency changes.
The approval has in a system place.
We are a system in place yesterday.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The natural pattern is have a system in place for + noun or -ing form.

assessment.retellingPrompt: Without looking at the full transcript, retell the episode in 80–120 words using this structure: (1) assumption—who customers think receives a tip; (2) problem—different systems and possible unfairness; (3) solution and change—how a tronc works as society becomes cashless. Phrase bank: “not always the case”, “have a system in place”, “pool tips and service charges”. Use at least two phrases naturally. Simple, accurate sentences are enough.
referencePoints: Tipping is discretionary in the UK, but it is often expected in restaurants.
The person who serves the food does not necessarily keep the tip.
Restaurants use different systems, and workers may feel that some methods divide tips unfairly.
A tronc is a special arrangement that keeps collected tips in a separate account and applies the correct tax treatment.
A tronc can pool tips and service charges and distribute them among staff according to the business's protocol.
The growth of card payments and a cashless society means more tips now pass through digital payment systems.
